mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP (GDPC1) indicates a strong economy, leading to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over 60 days in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4% signals a strong labor market, boosting consumer spending and S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: UNRATE falls below 4% but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates supply-side strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Industrial production growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over 60 days in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 1400 signals strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Housing starts exceed 1400 but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicate strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Both RSAFS and HOUST increase but S&P 500 returns are negative over 60 days in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4% may slow economic growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS exceeds 4% but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in CPI (CPIAUCSL) above 335 indicates inflation, potentially leading to rate hikes and negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: CPI exceeds 335 but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in employment (PAYEMS) alongside a decrease in retail sales (RSAFS) may indicate labor market strength but weak demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: PAYEMS increases while RSAFS decreases but S&P 500 returns are positive over 60 days in more than 40% of cases.
